functional.title: Verify API documentation page is accessible and loads correctly
preconditions: User is logged into the application with a valid account
API documentation has been published and deployed to the documentation portal
User has at least 'Viewer' or 'Developer' role permissions
Browser is a modern supported browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari latest)

steps.action: Navigate to the main application dashboard or home page
steps.expectedResult: Dashboard loads successfully with navigation menu visible

steps.action: Locate and click the 'Documentation' or 'API Docs' link in the main navigation menu or footer
steps.expectedResult: The API documentation landing page loads within 3 seconds, displaying the documentation title, version number, and table of contents

steps.action: Verify the page structure includes sections for Introduction, Authentication, Endpoints, Error Codes, and Rate Limits
steps.expectedResult: All major sections are listed in the table of contents / sidebar navigation and each section heading is visible

steps.action: Scroll through the entire documentation page from top to bottom
steps.expectedResult: All content renders correctly with no broken images, missing text, or layout issues. Code examples are displayed in formatted code blocks

steps.action: Check the documentation version number displayed in the header or footer area
steps.expectedResult: Version number matches the latest published release version (e.g., 'v1.0.0' or the current sprint version)

postconditions: API documentation page remains loaded and accessible for further browsing
No console errors related to documentation rendering are present in browser developer tools
User session remains active and authenticated

functional.title: Verify all API endpoints are documented with correct HTTP methods, paths, and descriptions
preconditions: API documentation page is loaded and accessible
User is authenticated with Developer or Admin role
A reference list of all implemented API endpoints is available for cross-checking
The API service is running and endpoints are deployed

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Endpoints' or 'API Reference' section of the documentation
steps.expectedResult: A categorized list of all API endpoints is displayed, grouped by resource or domain (e.g., Users, Orders, Products)

steps.action: For each endpoint listed, verify the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is clearly indicated with a color-coded badge or label
steps.expectedResult: Each endpoint displays the correct HTTP method badge (e.g., green for GET, blue for POST, orange for PUT, red for DELETE) matching the reference list

steps.action: Click on the first GET endpoint (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users') to expand its details
steps.expectedResult: Endpoint detail section expands showing: full URL path, description of what the endpoint does, request parameters (query/path), request headers, and example response with status codes

steps.action: Click on a POST endpoint (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/users') to expand its details
steps.expectedResult: Endpoint detail section shows: request body schema with field names, data types, required/optional indicators, example request payload in JSON format, and example success/error responses

steps.action: Cross-reference the documented endpoints against the reference list of implemented endpoints
steps.expectedResult: Every implemented endpoint appears in the documentation with no missing or extra undocumented endpoints

steps.action: Verify at least one endpoint from each HTTP method type (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) has a complete example request and response
steps.expectedResult: Each method type has at least one fully documented example with realistic sample data in both request and response bodies

postconditions: All API endpoints are confirmed documented and match the implemented API surface
No discrepancies found between documentation and actual API implementation
Documentation page remains stable with no rendering issues after expanding/collapsing multiple endpoints

functional.title: Verify authentication section documents all supported auth methods with examples
preconditions: API documentation page is loaded and accessible
User is authenticated and on the documentation portal
The API supports at least one authentication method (e.g., API Key, OAuth 2.0, Bearer Token)

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Authentication' section in the documentation sidebar or table of contents
steps.expectedResult: Authentication section loads displaying an overview of supported authentication methods

steps.action: Verify the section lists all supported authentication mechanisms (e.g., API Key, Bearer Token, OAuth 2.0)
steps.expectedResult: Each authentication method is listed with a clear heading, description of when to use it, and security considerations

steps.action: Review the API Key authentication subsection for instructions on how to obtain and use an API key
steps.expectedResult: Documentation includes: step-by-step instructions to generate an API key, where to include the key in requests (header name e.g., 'X-API-Key' or 'Authorization'), and a curl/HTTP example showing the header in use

steps.action: Review the Bearer Token / OAuth 2.0 subsection for token acquisition flow
steps.expectedResult: Documentation includes: token endpoint URL, required parameters (client_id, client_secret, grant_type), example token request, example token response with access_token and expiry, and how to include the token in subsequent API calls

steps.action: Copy the example curl command from the authentication section and verify it is syntactically correct
steps.expectedResult: The curl command is properly formatted, uses correct syntax, includes placeholder values clearly marked (e.g., '<YOUR_API_KEY>'), and can be pasted into a terminal without syntax errors after replacing placeholders

postconditions: Authentication documentation is confirmed complete with all supported methods
Example code snippets are syntactically valid and copy-pasteable
User understands the full authentication flow from reading the documentation alone

functional.title: Verify user guide section provides step-by-step getting started instructions
preconditions: Documentation portal is accessible and loaded
User guide section has been published alongside the API documentation
User is a new developer with no prior knowledge of the system

steps.action: Navigate to the 'User Guide' or 'Getting Started' section from the documentation home page or sidebar navigation
steps.expectedResult: User guide landing page loads with a clear 'Getting Started' heading and an overview of what the guide covers

steps.action: Verify the guide includes a 'Prerequisites' or 'Before You Begin' section
steps.expectedResult: Prerequisites section lists required tools, accounts, permissions, SDK versions, and any environment setup needed before using the API

steps.action: Follow the 'Quick Start' or 'First API Call' tutorial step by step
steps.expectedResult: The tutorial provides numbered steps including: 1) How to sign up/get credentials, 2) How to authenticate, 3) How to make a first API call, 4) How to interpret the response. Each step has clear instructions and expected outcomes

steps.action: Verify that code examples in the user guide are provided in at least two programming languages (e.g., curl, Python, JavaScript)
steps.expectedResult: Code examples are available in multiple languages with a language selector/tabs, and each example is complete and runnable

steps.action: Check that the user guide includes a 'Common Use Cases' or 'Tutorials' section beyond the quick start
steps.expectedResult: At least 2-3 common use case tutorials are documented (e.g., 'Creating a resource', 'Searching and filtering', 'Handling pagination') with full code examples and explanations

steps.action: Verify the user guide includes a 'Troubleshooting' or 'FAQ' section
steps.expectedResult: Troubleshooting section lists at least 5 common issues with solutions (e.g., '401 Unauthorized - Check your API key', '429 Too Many Requests - Implement rate limiting backoff')

postconditions: User guide is confirmed to provide a complete onboarding experience from zero to first successful API call
All code examples in the user guide are syntactically correct and include comments
Troubleshooting section covers the most common developer pain points

functional.title: Verify API documentation includes complete request and response schema definitions
preconditions: API documentation is loaded on the documentation portal
At least one resource endpoint (e.g., /api/v1/users) is documented
OpenAPI/Swagger specification or equivalent schema reference is available for validation

steps.action: Navigate to a POST endpoint documentation (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/users - Create User')
steps.expectedResult: Endpoint detail page loads showing request body schema section

steps.action: Review the request body schema and verify it includes: field name, data type, required/optional flag, description, constraints (min/max length, regex pattern, enum values)
steps.expectedResult: Each field in the request body is documented with all attributes. For example: 'email' - type: string, required: true, format: email, description: 'User email address', maxLength: 255

steps.action: Review the response schema for a successful response (HTTP 200/201)
steps.expectedResult: Success response schema shows the complete response object structure with field names, data types, descriptions, and an example JSON response body

steps.action: Review the error response schemas (HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 500)
steps.expectedResult: Each error status code has a documented response schema showing the error object structure (e.g., {"error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Email is required", "details": [...]}})

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Models' or 'Schemas' section of the documentation if available
steps.expectedResult: A dedicated section lists all data models/schemas used across the API with their complete field definitions, relationships, and example objects

steps.action: Cross-reference one documented schema against an actual API response by making a test API call
steps.expectedResult: The actual API response structure matches the documented schema exactly - same field names, same data types, same nesting structure

postconditions: All request and response schemas are confirmed complete and accurate
Schema documentation matches the actual API behavior
No undocumented fields exist in actual API responses

functional.title: Verify documentation search functionality returns relevant results
preconditions: Documentation portal is loaded and accessible
Search functionality is implemented on the documentation site
Documentation content has been indexed for search

steps.action: Locate the search bar on the documentation page (typically in the header or sidebar)
steps.expectedResult: Search input field is visible with a placeholder text like 'Search documentation...' or a magnifying glass icon

steps.action: Type 'authentication' into the search bar and press Enter or wait for auto-complete results
steps.expectedResult: Search results appear showing relevant documentation sections related to authentication, including the Authentication section, any endpoints requiring auth, and related user guide sections

steps.action: Click on the first search result
steps.expectedResult: User is navigated directly to the relevant section of the documentation with the search term highlighted or the section scrolled into view

steps.action: Return to the search bar and type a specific endpoint path (e.g., '/api/v1/users')
steps.expectedResult: Search results show the specific endpoint documentation page and any user guide sections that reference this endpoint

steps.action: Search for a term that does not exist in the documentation (e.g., 'xyznonexistent123')
steps.expectedResult: A 'No results found' message is displayed with a suggestion to browse the table of contents or refine the search query

steps.action: Clear the search bar and verify the documentation returns to its normal state
steps.expectedResult: Search results are cleared and the documentation page displays its default content/navigation

postconditions: Search functionality is confirmed working with relevant result ranking
Search handles both found and not-found scenarios gracefully
Navigation from search results correctly links to the appropriate documentation sections

functional.title: Verify documentation navigation sidebar and table of contents work correctly
preconditions: Documentation portal is loaded in a desktop browser
All documentation sections have been published
Sidebar navigation is visible on the left side of the page

steps.action: Observe the sidebar navigation on the documentation page
steps.expectedResult: Sidebar displays a hierarchical table of contents with expandable/collapsible sections including: Introduction, Authentication, API Reference (with sub-items for each resource), User Guide, Error Codes, Rate Limits, Changelog

steps.action: Click on 'API Reference' in the sidebar to expand its sub-sections
steps.expectedResult: Sub-sections expand showing individual resource categories (e.g., Users, Orders, Products) with further expandable endpoint listings

steps.action: Click on a specific endpoint link in the sidebar (e.g., 'GET /users')
steps.expectedResult: The main content area scrolls to or loads the selected endpoint documentation. The sidebar item is highlighted/active to indicate current location

steps.action: Scroll down the main content area past several sections
steps.expectedResult: The sidebar navigation highlights the current section as the user scrolls, providing a visual indicator of the reader's position in the documentation

steps.action: Click the 'Back to top' link or the documentation logo/title to return to the top of the page
steps.expectedResult: Page scrolls smoothly back to the top and the sidebar resets to show the top-level navigation items

steps.action: Click on 'Changelog' or 'Version History' in the sidebar
steps.expectedResult: Changelog section loads showing a chronological list of API changes with dates, version numbers, and descriptions of what was added, changed, deprecated, or removed

postconditions: All sidebar navigation links correctly route to their respective documentation sections
Active section highlighting in sidebar accurately reflects the user's current position
No broken links or dead-end navigation paths exist in the sidebar

functional.title: Verify error codes and status codes are comprehensively documented
preconditions: API documentation is loaded and accessible
Error codes section exists in the documentation
A reference list of all API error codes is available for cross-checking

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Error Codes' or 'Status Codes' section in the documentation
steps.expectedResult: A dedicated section loads displaying a table or list of all HTTP status codes and custom error codes used by the API

steps.action: Verify standard HTTP status codes are documented (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429, 500, 503)
steps.expectedResult: Each status code is listed with: numeric code, standard name (e.g., '400 Bad Request'), description of when the API returns this code, and an example response body

steps.action: Verify custom/application-specific error codes are documented if applicable
steps.expectedResult: Custom error codes (e.g., 'INVALID_EMAIL_FORMAT', 'RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED') are listed with: error code string, human-readable message, description, and suggested resolution

steps.action: Check that the error response format/schema is documented
steps.expectedResult: A standard error response format is defined showing the JSON structure (e.g., {"error": {"code": "string", "message": "string", "details": []}}) with field descriptions

steps.action: Verify rate limiting error (429) documentation includes rate limit details
steps.expectedResult: Rate limiting section documents: request limits per time window, rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset), and recommended retry/backoff strategy

postconditions: All error codes returned by the API are documented with clear descriptions
Developers can understand and handle every possible error response from the documentation alone
Rate limiting behavior is clearly explained with actionable guidance

functional.title: Verify interactive 'Try It Out' or API playground functionality works correctly
preconditions: Documentation portal includes an interactive API testing feature (e.g., Swagger UI 'Try it out', Postman-style playground)
User is authenticated on the documentation portal
API backend service is running and accessible from the documentation portal
Test/sandbox environment credentials are available

steps.action: Navigate to a GET endpoint documentation page (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users')
steps.expectedResult: Endpoint documentation is displayed with a 'Try It Out' or 'Send Request' button visible

steps.action: Click the 'Try It Out' button
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint section transforms into an interactive form with editable fields for path parameters, query parameters, and headers. An 'Execute' or 'Send' button appears

steps.action: Enter valid authentication credentials in the Authorization header field (e.g., 'Bearer <test_token>') and click 'Execute'
steps.expectedResult: The API call is made and the response is displayed below showing: HTTP status code (e.g., 200), response headers, response body in formatted JSON, and the actual curl command that was executed

steps.action: Navigate to a POST endpoint and click 'Try It Out'
steps.expectedResult: An editable request body text area appears pre-populated with the example request JSON from the documentation

steps.action: Modify the pre-populated request body with valid test data and click 'Execute'
steps.expectedResult: The POST request is sent, and the response shows HTTP 201 Created with the created resource in the response body

steps.action: Remove the Authorization header and click 'Execute' on any endpoint
steps.expectedResult: The response shows HTTP 401 Unauthorized with the documented error response format, demonstrating the authentication requirement

postconditions: Interactive API testing feature is confirmed functional for both GET and POST methods
Responses from the playground match the documented response schemas
Any test data created during playground testing is in the sandbox/test environment only

functional.title: Verify documentation versioning and version switching functionality
preconditions: Multiple versions of the API documentation exist (e.g., v1.0, v1.1, v2.0)
Documentation portal supports version switching
User is on the documentation portal viewing the latest version

steps.action: Locate the version selector dropdown or toggle on the documentation page (typically in the header near the title)
steps.expectedResult: A version selector is visible displaying the current version (e.g., 'v2.0 (latest)') with a dropdown arrow or similar indicator

steps.action: Click the version selector to open the dropdown
steps.expectedResult: A dropdown list appears showing all available documentation versions (e.g., 'v2.0 (latest)', 'v1.1', 'v1.0') with the current version highlighted

steps.action: Select an older version (e.g., 'v1.0') from the dropdown
steps.expectedResult: The documentation page reloads or updates to show the v1.0 documentation. The version indicator updates to show 'v1.0'. A banner or notice may appear indicating this is not the latest version

steps.action: Verify the content of the older version differs from the latest (e.g., fewer endpoints, different schemas)
steps.expectedResult: The older version documentation reflects the API state at that version - endpoints added in later versions are not present, and schemas match the v1.0 specification

steps.action: Click the 'View latest version' link or switch back to the latest version using the version selector
steps.expectedResult: Documentation returns to the latest version with all current endpoints and schemas. Any 'outdated version' banner is removed

postconditions: Version switching is confirmed functional with accurate content per version
Users are clearly informed when viewing an older version of the documentation
Deep links to specific documentation sections maintain version context

functional.title: Verify code examples can be copied to clipboard successfully
preconditions: Documentation portal is loaded with code examples visible
Browser supports clipboard API
At least one endpoint with code examples in multiple languages is displayed

steps.action: Navigate to any endpoint documentation that contains a code example (e.g., a curl command example)
steps.expectedResult: Code example is displayed in a formatted code block with syntax highlighting and a 'Copy' button (clipboard icon) visible in the top-right corner of the code block

steps.action: Click the 'Copy' button on the code example
steps.expectedResult: A visual confirmation appears (e.g., the button text changes to 'Copied!' or a green checkmark appears, or a toast notification says 'Copied to clipboard')

steps.action: Open a text editor or terminal and paste (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V) the copied content
steps.expectedResult: The pasted content exactly matches the code example from the documentation, including proper formatting, indentation, and all characters

steps.action: Switch the code example language tab to a different language (e.g., from 'curl' to 'Python')
steps.expectedResult: The code block updates to show the equivalent example in Python with proper syntax highlighting for Python

steps.action: Click the 'Copy' button on the Python code example and paste it into a text editor
steps.expectedResult: The Python code is correctly copied with proper indentation and can be saved as a .py file and executed (after replacing placeholder values)

postconditions: Copy functionality works for all code example languages
Copied code maintains proper formatting and is immediately usable
Copy button visual feedback resets after a few seconds for subsequent copies

functional.title: Verify documentation is accessible to different user roles with appropriate content visibility
preconditions: Documentation portal supports role-based access if applicable
Test accounts exist for different roles: Public/Anonymous user, Authenticated Developer, Admin user
Some documentation sections may be restricted (e.g., Admin API endpoints)

steps.action: Access the documentation portal as an unauthenticated/public user (not logged in)
steps.expectedResult: Public documentation sections are visible (e.g., Introduction, Getting Started, Public API endpoints). If all docs are public, the full documentation loads. If some are restricted, a login prompt or 'restricted' indicator appears for protected sections

steps.action: Log in as a user with 'Developer' role and navigate to the documentation portal
steps.expectedResult: All standard API documentation sections are accessible including endpoints, authentication guide, user guide, and code examples

steps.action: Log in as a user with 'Admin' role and navigate to the documentation portal
steps.expectedResult: All documentation sections are accessible including any admin-only API endpoints or configuration guides that may be hidden from regular developers

steps.action: As an Admin user, navigate to an admin-only section (e.g., 'Admin API - User Management')
steps.expectedResult: Admin API documentation loads with endpoints for user management, system configuration, and other administrative operations

steps.action: Log out and attempt to directly access the admin documentation URL
steps.expectedResult: User is redirected to a login page or receives a 403 Forbidden message indicating they do not have permission to view this section

postconditions: Role-based documentation access is confirmed working correctly
No sensitive admin documentation is exposed to unauthorized users
Public documentation remains accessible without authentication

functional.title: Verify documentation renders correctly on mobile devices and tablets
preconditions: Documentation portal is loaded and accessible
Mobile device or browser developer tools with device emulation are available
Documentation site is expected to be responsive

steps.action: Open the documentation portal on a mobile device (or use Chrome DevTools to emulate iPhone 14 at 390x844 resolution)
steps.expectedResult: Documentation page loads with a responsive layout - sidebar navigation collapses into a hamburger menu, content fills the screen width, and text is readable without horizontal scrolling

steps.action: Tap the hamburger menu icon to open the navigation sidebar
steps.expectedResult: Sidebar slides in from the left as an overlay, displaying the full table of contents with all sections accessible via touch

steps.action: Tap on an endpoint section in the mobile navigation
steps.expectedResult: Navigation closes and the main content scrolls to the selected endpoint section. Content is properly formatted for mobile width

steps.action: View a code example block on the mobile layout
steps.expectedResult: Code block is horizontally scrollable within its container (not causing the entire page to scroll horizontally). Copy button is accessible via touch

steps.action: Switch to tablet emulation (e.g., iPad at 768x1024) and verify the layout
steps.expectedResult: Documentation displays in a tablet-optimized layout - sidebar may be visible alongside content, or accessible via toggle. All content is readable and interactive elements are touch-friendly

postconditions: Documentation is confirmed responsive and usable across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports
No content is cut off or inaccessible on smaller screens
All interactive features (navigation, copy, search, try-it-out) work on touch devices

functional.title: Verify documentation includes pagination, filtering, and sorting parameter documentation
preconditions: API documentation is loaded and accessible
API supports list endpoints with pagination, filtering, and sorting capabilities
At least one list endpoint (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users') is documented

steps.action: Navigate to a list endpoint documentation (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users')
steps.expectedResult: Endpoint documentation shows query parameters section with pagination, filtering, and sorting parameters listed

steps.action: Review the pagination parameters documentation
steps.expectedResult: Pagination parameters are documented including: 'page' or 'offset' (type: integer, default value, description), 'limit' or 'per_page' (type: integer, default value, max value, description). Example: 'GET /api/v1/users?page=2&limit=25'

steps.action: Review the filtering parameters documentation
steps.expectedResult: Filter parameters are documented with supported filter fields (e.g., 'status=active', 'created_after=2024-01-01'), supported operators, and example filter queries

steps.action: Review the sorting parameters documentation
steps.expectedResult: Sort parameters are documented showing: sort field parameter name (e.g., 'sort_by'), supported sort fields (e.g., 'created_at', 'name'), sort direction (e.g., 'order=asc|desc'), and example: 'GET /api/v1/users?sort_by=created_at&order=desc'

steps.action: Review the paginated response format documentation
steps.expectedResult: Response format shows pagination metadata in the response body or headers (e.g., 'total_count', 'page', 'per_page', 'total_pages', or Link headers for cursor-based pagination) with a complete example response

postconditions: Pagination, filtering, and sorting are fully documented for all list endpoints
Default values and maximum limits are clearly stated
Example queries demonstrate real-world usage patterns

functional.title: Verify documentation deep links and URL anchors work for sharing specific sections
preconditions: Documentation portal is loaded and accessible
Documentation sections have anchor links / fragment identifiers in the URL
A second browser tab or incognito window is available for testing

steps.action: Navigate to a specific section in the documentation (e.g., the 'Authentication' section) and observe the URL in the browser address bar
steps.expectedResult: The URL updates to include a fragment identifier or path segment for the current section (e.g., '/docs#authentication' or '/docs/authentication')

steps.action: Hover over a section heading (e.g., 'Bearer Token Authentication') and look for a link/anchor icon
steps.expectedResult: A link icon (chain link or '#' symbol) appears next to the heading, indicating a deep link is available for this specific subsection

steps.action: Click the anchor icon to copy the deep link URL, or right-click and select 'Copy link address'
steps.expectedResult: The URL is copied to clipboard with the specific section anchor (e.g., '/docs/authentication#bearer-token')

steps.action: Open a new browser tab or incognito window and paste the copied deep link URL into the address bar, then press Enter
steps.expectedResult: The documentation page loads and automatically scrolls to the exact section referenced by the anchor link. The 'Bearer Token Authentication' heading is visible at or near the top of the viewport

steps.action: Share the deep link URL via a messaging tool and open it from the message
steps.expectedResult: The link opens the documentation at the exact referenced section, confirming deep links are shareable and persistent

postconditions: Deep links correctly navigate to specific documentation sections
URLs are human-readable and descriptive
Deep links remain stable across page refreshes and browser sessions
